rtl_result.summary: Cannot implement/repair manifest modules because frozen artifacts do not define explicit internal module port contracts for input_loader, gemm_core_seq, postproc_relu_bias, output_streamer, and local_memories. Existing RTL uses wildcard top-level coupling, which is not a frozen interface contract and is insufficiently specified for deterministic compliant repair.

contract_checks.requirement: Implement only frozen architecture/interface semantics without inventing missing contracts
contract_checks.evidence: Frozen manifest lists module names/responsibilities/parameters but omits required port lists and signal-level internal interfaces between modules.

contract_checks.requirement: FUNCTIONAL_REPAIR may modify affected modules only, preserving external protected interface
contract_checks.evidence: Repair requires defining new internal ports/signals across all affected modules; these interface decisions are currently unspecified by frozen artifacts.

contract_checks.requirement: Return ARCHITECTURE_CONFLICT when architectural/interface decision is missing
contract_checks.evidence: Missing internal module interface definitions block compliant RTL implementation without making new architect-owned decisions.

architecture_conflict.issue: No explicit frozen port contracts for non-top manifest modules; deterministic, synthesizable, contract-faithful implementation requires architect-specified ports (names, directions, widths, handshake timing, memory read/write interfaces, done/error signaling boundaries).
architecture_conflict.evidence: module_manifest provides responsibilities/dependencies/parameters only; existing stub comments ('ports via top .*') and wildcard instantiation are not authoritative frozen contracts and cannot be safely redefined in repair.
architecture_conflict.requested_architect_decision: Provide complete frozen port lists for each manifest module (including all control, memory, data, counter/address, done/error, and ready/valid-related signals), plus any required latency/validity rules for those internal interfaces.

known_risks: Attempting patch without frozen internal ports would introduce non-authorized architectural/interface choices and may violate verification expectations.
